issues.description: The problem statement/UML declares numberOfTutors as type int, but the solution implementation defines the attribute as short (private short numberOfTutors). This type mismatch between the specification and the reference solution can confuse students about the intended attribute type and may lead to inconsistent constructor/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the numberOfTutors field in the solution to int to match the UML/specification (e.g. private int numberOfTutors;). Update related constructor parameter and setter to use int as well so all artifacts use the same type.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a constructor that initializes all attributes in the order given by the UML (last parameter numberOfTutors of type int), but the solution's constructor declares the final parameter as short (short numberOfTutors). This constructor parameter type mismatch deviates from the specified design and can mislead students about the correct constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution constructor signature to accept an int for numberOfTutors (e.g. public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors)) to match the UML and problem description.

issues.description: The problem expects standard setters for each attribute (with parameter types matching the attribute types described in the UML). In the solution, setNumberOfTutors accepts a short parameter (setNumberOfTutors(short numberOfTutors)), while the UML implies an int parameter. This method parameter type mismatch can confuse students implementing the setter and lead to inconsistent API usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the setter signature in the solution to accept an int (e.g. public void setNumberOfTutors(int numberOfTutors)) and ensure the backing field is also int, so the setter's parameter type matches the UML and other getters/setters.
